title: Palindrome test phase
statement: Let $x$ be a binary word, and let $r,i\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $i\le |x|$ and $|x|=i+r$. Starting in the three-state palindrome machine's test configuration on input $x$, with the input head at position $i+1$, the work head at integer position $|x|-1-i$, and the first $|x|$ bits copied, after $r+1$ steps the machine is halted and its output is the one-bit word whose bit is true exactly when $x$ agrees with its reversal at every position $j$ satisfying $i\le j<|x|$.
replaced:
Let $x$ be a binary word of length $n$, and let $r$ and $i \le n$ satisfy
$n = i + r$. Running the three-state palindrome machine for $r+1$ steps from the
test-state configuration on input $x$ with input head at cell $i+1$, all $n$ bits
copied, and work head at the integer cell $n-1-i$ produces a halted
configuration whose output is the single bit \emph{true} if every opposing pair
of $x$ at or after position $i$ agrees (the $j$-th bit of $x^{R}$ equals the
$j$-th bit of $x$ for all $i \le j < n$), and \emph{false} otherwise.
